units.text: The most structured junior-year requirement in this set

A demanding, open transcript: required AP exams, a full published quintile table, and published AP exam and Scholar counts. It comes with the thinnest learning-support disclosure among the schools on this site.

No AP Scholar tier counts are published. Instead, the profile gives results by exam (94% scoring 3+ across 1,184 exams in 2026). That tells you more. But it means the Scholar/Scholar with Distinction ledger other schools show cannot be built here.
The profile answers the questions a family actually asks — and the tuition structure answers one no other school on this roster raises.

Uniquely among the schools here, the ERP explicitly **“assists in requesting accommodations with the College Board, ACT, and IB”** — the hand-off into admissions testing is stated rather than left implicit.

**Michelle Donah**, Upper School Learning Specialist, and **Jennifer Ridenhour**, Upper School Dean of Academic Support. That is substantial staffing for 421 Upper School students. It is also some of the best-documented learning support of the schools on this site.

A stable program that is honest by design. Students keep the same counselor for all four years. It also has a published course-load ceiling, real research defences and a genuine list of where graduates enrolled. But it shares less about outcomes than its larger peers.
One dedicated college counseling director — in her 23rd year at the school — for 85 seniors, the heaviest caseload in this comparison.
The differentiators are depth stories: a department no other school has, a housing build on Pine Ridge, and college credit from the PCA’s own college.
A named high-school department with its own director (Dr. Rebeca Burnett) — unique among these schools
The heaviest caseload in this comparison

Every verdict point below is about what the school does. A family that evaluates schools on published outcome metrics will find less here than anywhere else in this set, which puts the burden of verification on the tour.
Course planning begins four years before applications, and the ~18:1 senior caseload is among the lowest on this roster.
Uploaded to myCCS. "For families with two households, please upload a copy of your custody agreements" — a document the other Charlotte schools do not ask for up front.

Aid is **need-based** and runs through **FACTS**, with **a new application required each year**. There is also one step you must complete first, and it is unique among the Charlotte schools. To be eligible for aid from Covenant Day, **families must first provide proof of application for the NC Opportunity Scholarship**. File the aid application **at the same time as the admissions application**, not after a decision. Enrollment carries a **$1,000 non-refundable deposit** per student, applied toward tuition. **The FACTS application fee and any reduced deposit for aid applicants are not published**.

Four bands cover all fourteen grade levels from TK through Grade 12, with no gap and no overlap. TK and Kindergarten each have their own price, Grades 1–5 share one rate, and Grades 6–12 share another. The school lists what tuition includes: student iPads and all technology · all textbooks (including A.P. textbooks) · A.P. exam fees · most class field trips · all Lower School student supplies. Among the schools on this site, this kind of list is published less consistently than any other item these reports track.

Through the 2026–27 cycle, every applicant family had to **also apply to the North Carolina Opportunity Scholarship Program**. Applications for that state program opened 2 February. No other school on this site made its own aid application depend on a state application. **It no longer applies**: the school's live tuition page (retrieved 14 Sep 2026) does not mention it. That fits the school's own note that NC Opportunity Scholarship participation ends after 2025–26.

No other school on this site prices tuition this way: **price depends on parish participation, not on grade level or financial need**. A participating Catholic family pays **$15,041**, and a community family pays **$21,562**, for the same seat in the same classroom. That is a **$6,521 difference, roughly 30%**. CCHS is a 9–12 school, so there is no ladder of grade bands at all. These three rows are the entire schedule.

Need is assessed through the **Clarity** application (**$65** fee). **FACTS appears in this system only as the payment processor**, not as the tool that assesses need. That is an easy mix-up with real consequences, because some other schools on this site use FACTS Grant & Aid to assess need. **TADS is not used.**
Published tuition by grade band — the lowest top rate in this comparison

The school states what tuition includes: on-campus computers/iPads · technology expenses · school retreats and required field trips · science lab and elective fees · most athletic expenses. Several other schools on this site do not publish a list like this.
Proof of application for the **NC Opportunity Scholarship** is mandatory before any CDS aid is considered — a hard gate no peer school here imposes

Covenant Day is a ministry of Christ Covenant Church (PCA), and the IRS designates it a **religious organization not required to file Form 990** (EIN 56-1656570, exempt since 1989). ProPublica’s Nonprofit Explorer confirms no filing exists. Most other schools on this site file a Form 990, so their aid totals can be checked against a return. Here there is **no filing to check**. The gap comes from how the school is set up, not from a page that has yet to be found.
top band — the lowest top tuition in this comparison

The school publishes no rate history, because each year's table replaces the one before. But archived copies show 2022–23 onward. Every division has risen a near-flat **~4.5% a year** since 2023–24, one of the steadiest patterns among the schools on this site. Early Childhood years are left out of the run above, because the number of years a child spends in that band varies.

Carmel Christian is a ministry of Carmel Baptist Church. As a church-affiliated organization, it is **not required to file Form 990**, and ProPublica returns no filing for the school itself. Most other schools on this site file a Form 990, so their aid totals can be checked against a return. Here there is **no filing to check**. The gap comes from how the school is set up, not from a page that has yet to be found.

Hickory Grove Christian is a ministry of **Hickory Grove Baptist Church**. As a church-affiliated organization, it is **not required to file Form 990**, and ProPublica returns no filing for the church as a school operator. Most other schools on this site file a Form 990, so their aid totals can be checked against a return. Here there is **no filing to check**. The gap comes from how the school is set up, not from a page that has yet to be found.
Create an account with **Clarity**, not FACTS or SSS. Clarity is the aid platform most schools on this site use.
The school states aid of **up to 80% of tuition** for Kindergarten through grade 12. That is a real ceiling a family can plan against, and few schools on this roster publish one at all.

This is the thinnest section of Gaston Day’s public record. None of these appears anywhere on the public site: plan names · an installment schedule · plan fees · a card-processing surcharge · a deposit amount · a late-payment policy · withdrawal or refund terms · a tuition-insurance or refund-plan option. Most other schools on this site publish at least the number of installments.

Trinity prices the activity fee **per grade**, one of very few schools on this roster to do so. It runs from **$210** in Kindergarten to **$1,045** in 8th grade, rising at grade 4 (**$545**) and again at grade 6 (**$965**). What the fee buys is not stated.

A genuine three-point series, which few schools on this roster publish: **26% / $2.1 million in 2023-24**, **29% / $2 million in 2025-26**, and **31% / $2,139,114 in 2026-27**. The share has risen steadily while the dollar total dipped and recovered. The 2026-27 figures carry the school's own qualifier, "**(excludes Tuition Remission)**" — employee tuition benefits sit outside this number.
The deepest arts facilities of any school in this set, a dual AP-and-IB ceiling, and a statewide-honored theatre director — with a Blumey record that has cooled sharply.
One Fine Arts credit is required to graduate, and worship bands run at both middle and high school — a rung no other school here has.
A theatre program with a genuine, recently converted Blumey win, sitting on a leaner music and visual-arts footprint than its regional peers.
The deepest published affinity structure in this comparison set, built out steadily from 1995 onward — though the school’s own live site no longer lists it.
Charlotte Latin publishes markedly less on this than its peers: no roster page, no counts, and no divisional breakout.
Two recognition societies plus a theatre society — and, uniquely in this comparison, published induction criteria and a published induction count.
The directory is one of the most transparent on this roster — most entries publish a written purpose, a staff advisor and where the club actually meets.
Twelve honor societies — the widest span in this comparison, reaching social studies, mathematics, English, journalism, three arts and three world languages.
The smallest school in this comparison publishes the least overall — but its civic programming is specific, externally validated and genuinely unusual.

Diocesan coverage records a North Carolina state runner-up finish and a Program Oral Interpretation state champion. That coverage is from 2017, older than any competitive result shipped for another school here, so no current standing can be claimed. The club meets in the CCHS Media Center under Mrs. Jennifer Taylor.
A distinctive network the others do not have
The profile gives it a stand-alone descriptive block — a transcript line no other Charlotte-area applicant carries
A requirement unique in this series — and since withdrawn

The strongest tuition history of the four schools in this series. Every band rose **$850** into 2024–25, **$1,500** into 2025–26 and **$950** into 2026–27 — a flat dollar increment each time, totaling **+$3,300** per band, or 18.33% at the lowest band against 13.89% at the highest.
The worship-music spine is unique here
Earliest start on the roster
